questions.q: Why does the prophet want to weep?
questions.a: He wants to weep because so many of his people have been killed.

questions.q: Why does the prophet want to abandon his people?
questions.a: He wants to abandon them because they are adulterers and traitors.

questions.q: What do the sinful people say?
questions.a: They say false things.

questions.q: Why should each of them guard against their neighbors and brothers?
questions.a: They should guard against them because every brother and neighbor is a deceiver.

questions.q: Why are the people exhausted?
questions.a: They are exhausted from committing iniquity.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say the people refuse to do?
questions.a: They refuse to know him because of their deceit.

questions.q: Why does Yahweh want to test his people?
questions.a: He wants to test them because they lie to their neighbors.

questions.q: Why does Yahweh want to test his people?
questions.a: He wants to test them because they lie to their neighbors.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to the people because of these things?
questions.a: He will punish them and take revenge on their nation.

questions.q: What will the prophet sing?
questions.a: He will sing funeral songs and mourning songs for the mountains and the meadows.

questions.q: What will Yahweh make of Jerusalem and Judah?
questions.a: He will turn them into ruined places.

questions.q: What will the land be like after it has perished?
questions.a: It will be like the wilderness, and no one will pass through it.

questions.q: What have the people done to displease Yahweh?
questions.a: They have abandoned his law and they do not listen to him.

questions.q: What have the people done instead of following Yahweh’s law?
questions.a: They have followed their own stubborn hearts and worshiped the Baals, as their ancestors taught them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to the Israelites?
questions.a: He will make them as unhappy as people who have nothing but bitter things to eat and drink. Then he will drive them from their homes and have them killed.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to the Israelites?
questions.a: He will make them as unhappy as people who have nothing but bitter things to eat and drink. Then he will drive them from their homes and have them killed.

questions.q: What should the women who are skilled at lamenting do?
questions.a: They should sing sad songs so that the people will cry.

questions.q: How do the wailing people in Zion feel?
questions.a: They are greatly ashamed.

questions.q: What should the women teach their daughters?
questions.a: They should teach their daughters a mourning song.

questions.q: Who does the prophet say are going to die?
questions.a: Children and young men are going to die.

questions.q: In what way will the corpses be like dung and grain stalks?
questions.a: There will be no one to bury them.

questions.q: What should people be proud of?
questions.a: People should be proud that they know Yahweh.

questions.q: What should people be proud of?
questions.a: People should be proud that they know Yahweh.

questions.q: With what does Yahweh say that he acts?
questions.a: He acts with covenant loyalty, justice, and righteousness.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will happen to those who are circumcised only in their bodies?
questions.a: Yahweh says a time is coming when he will punish them.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh punish the other people?
questions.a: He will punish them because even their bodies are uncircumcised.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh punish the Israelites?
questions.a: He will punish the Israelites because they are circumcised only in their body and not in their heart.

commentary.text: The people are corrected, Jerusalem is destroyed. (Jer. 9:1-11) The captives suffer in a foreign land. (Jer. 9:12-22) God's loving-kindness, He threatens the enemies of his people. (Jer. 9:23-26)

Jer. 9:1-11 Jeremiah wept much, yet wished he could weep more, that he might rouse the people to a due sense of the hand of God. But even the desert, without communion with God, through Christ Jesus, and the influences of the Holy Spirit, must be a place for temptation and evil; while, with these blessings, we may live in holiness in crowded cities. The people accustomed their tongues to lies. So false were they, that a brother could not be trusted. In trading and bargaining they said any thing for their own advantage, though they knew it to be false. But God marked their sin. Where no knowledge of God is, what good can be expected? He has many ways of turning a fruitful land into barrenness for the wickedness of those that dwell therein.

Jer. 9:12-22 In Zion the voice of joy and praise used to be heard, while the people kept close to God; but sin has altered the sound, it is now the voice of lamentation. Unhumbled hearts lament their calamity, but not their sin, which is the cause of it. Let the doors be shut ever so fast, death steals upon us. It enters the palaces of princes and great men, though stately, strongly built, and guarded. Nor are those more safe that are abroad; death cuts off even the children from without, and the young men from the streets. Hearken to the word of the Lord, and mourn with godly sorrow. This alone can bring true comfort; and it can turn the heaviest afflictions into precious mercies.

Jer. 9:23-26 In this world of sin and sorrow, ending soon in death and judgement, how foolish for men to glory in their knowledge, health, strength, riches, or in any thing which leaves them under the dominion of sin and the wrath of God! and of which an account must hereafter be rendered; it will but increase their misery. Those are the true Israel who worship God in the Spirit, rejoice in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh. Let us prize the distinction which comes from God, and will last for ever. Let us seek it diligently.
